column1: # ZAP baseline rules for the showcase application (scripts/zap-baseline.sh).
# Tab separated: <rule id> <IGNORE|WARN|FAIL> <why>. A rule that is not
# listed keeps its default, which is WARN, and the scan runs with -I, so a
# warning never fails the job. Only the rules below with FAIL do.
# The FAIL list is short on purpose: it holds the headers and cookie
# attributes henri sets for every application, so the scan is a regression
# test of those defaults rather than an opinion about the showcase. A rule
# that fires on something deliberate is IGNORE, with the reason, so that a
# new warning stands out in the log instead of drowning.
# --- what henri promises: a regression fails the scan ----------------------

column3: Anti-clickjacking header: helmet sets X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN
Content-Security-Policy: henri builds one in base/headers.js
Cookie SameSite: henri.sid and henri.csrf are both SameSite=Lax
Anti-CSRF tokens: the double-submit cookie is mounted by 4.user.js

column1: # --- deliberate, and documented: not worth a line in the log ---------------

column3: Cookie No HttpOnly: henri.csrf is read by the browser on purpose (double submit)
Storable and cacheable content: the public pages are meant to be cached; noStore() covers a signed-in one
Source code disclosure (Python): fires on the inertia page props, which are JSON
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: helmet leaves COEP off, it breaks third party embeds
